checklist.evidence: int64 minor units plus an ISO 4217 currency code ... Rounding happens once, at the line item, half-up, and is documented.
Double-entry, append-only journal. Corrections are reversing entries; rows are never updated or deleted.
A timeout leads to a status query, never a blind retry; every attempt carries an idempotency key.
card data never touches our servers (PCI SAQ-A) ... We verify the signature, dedupe on event ID
A CI migration check rejects any table that has no `tenant_id` or no RLS policy.
Re-rating a closed period from raw events reproduces the invoiced amount to the cent.
Immutable price versions ... Each tenant has a configured anchor timezone for period boundaries.
Gapless invoice numbering per tenant: a sequence allocated at finalization, inside the transaction.
Dunning: a retry schedule configurable per tenant, `past_due` handling, and a cancel-or-pause policy.
Daily reconciliation of our ledger cash against Stripe balance transactions and payouts.
Buy: payment processing ... Build: ledger, catalog, subscriptions, rating, invoicing, dunning. Those are the product.

traps.evidence: the app role gets INSERT only on journal tables, plus a trigger that rejects UPDATE and DELETE.
store the raw payload, dedupe, process out of order, and pull from Stripe periodically to catch missed events.
card data never touches our servers (PCI SAQ-A)
Shared database and schema, `tenant_id` on every row, Postgres row-level security (RLS) enforced.

note: Strong, correctness-focused plan with excellent phasing, immutability, idempotency and reversibility reasoning; weak on cost, entitlements, and detailed tax/dunning/operations.
